{"notes": "VISIT 5 (ended 7:45). I can't tell who placed what, so this rests on the board, what people said, and whether the two matched.

Board: Essentially unchanged since visit 4. Start, both bodies, upper fin, tail loop and lower fin spur are dark. Still pale and disconnected: the pieces at x 21-23, y 11-13, the two loops at x 14-18, and maybe one piece near x 27, y 9. The upper fin looks dark and connected, so the 'break' and 'jam' the team described aren't visible to me. Ask what they actually saw. Counts of 152/207 (Sofia) and 146/208 (Hana) are roughly consistent.

Omar: Gave the most specific public status: bottom closed, plus two named fin defects (start of upper fin, jam past junction). Credited Sofia and offered help. Good diagnosis and collaboration. No private update. Ask whether those defects were real and whether he helped fix them.

Sofia: Publicly very active and coordinating. Admitted her earlier junction misreport, which is honest. Weaknesses: privately said she'd stay clear to avoid bumping teammates, but then went into the fin corner herself and told Hana and Jack to keep out. Her nudge placed nothing, and her diagnosis shifted from a 'stray at the junction' to a 'jammed domino at the fin start'. The outcome of the lift is unseen, and the pale clutter at x 21-23 is still there. Ask what she lifted and why the clutter remains.

Hana: Private updates were consistent with Sofia's and Omar's, but she said nothing publicly this visit. Her claim to be on the fin break has no visible result. Her 'coordinating' claim is unverified, and Sofia is the one doing the visible coordinating. Ask what she fixed.

Jack: Silent again, with no private update, and told to keep clear. No new evidence, so don't mark him down. Ask him at the review about the pale piece near x 27, y 9."}
